chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah who said:

I asked him about a man who had two wives, and each of them gave birth to a boy. So one of his wives went and breast-fed a girl from the people. Is it befitting for his son to marry this girl? He said: No, because she was breast-fed with the milk of the Sheikh (father).
ai.seo_question: Can a man's son marry a girl breast-fed by his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of milk kinship (radāʿ) by establishing that a wife’s nursing act confers the status of 'milk-daughter' upon the husband, thereby creating a marital prohibition for his biological son. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the direct causal link between the wet-nurse and the husband, distinguishing this from other kinship forms. The ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic principles of mahram relationships in family law.
